full.description: This is a low-power photomicrograph of a skin biopsy stained with hematoxylin and eosin. The section shows marked hyalinization and sclerosis of collagen extending through the dermis and into the subcutis. There is a prominent focal area of dense fibrous tissue and vascular alteration within the deeper layers. These histologic features are characteristic of morphea or localized scleroderma.

The findings are characteristic of localized scleroderma, or morphea, with associated vascular and structural tissue changes.

random.description: This is a micrograph of a skin biopsy sample stained with hematoxylin and eosin. The section shows the epidermis, dermis, and subcutaneous tissue with a prominent laminated, concentric dermal structure in the deeper dermis. This encapsulated, onion-like structure is characteristic of a Pacinian corpuscle. The specimen appears largely unremarkable regarding any significant pathologic changes within the skin architecture.
